newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stks close off, CANTV falls on rate fears.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stks close off, CANTV falls on rate fears.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed off in volatile trade on concern that delayed rate increases for national telephone company CANTV may dent its profits, traders said.

CANTV's drop came despite a company announcement Sunday that the terms of its 1991 contract with the Venezuelan government remain in force, with a 4.18 percent increase due in the second quarter based on inflation in the previous quarter. On Friday, the Venezuelan government said it will first negotiate with the telephone company on second quarter increases, seeking third party arbitration if the talks fail.
CANTV closed down 100.00 bolivars at 1920.00, pushing leading brokerage Merinvest's composite index down 0.80 percent to 95.18.

The bolsa's 19-share index, which does not include CANTV, meanwhile edged ahead 0.33 percent to close at 6,257.69 as 29.7 million shares traded, worth 2.5 billion bolivars ($5.24 million), according to preliminary figures from the exchange.
"It was a lazy market, with very little foreign interest," said Intervalores broker Ricardo Marino, who saw little chance of improvement over the week.
Last week, the bolsa dropped over seven percent on a heady cocktail of coup rumors, currency volatility and scares over the president's health.
"Some investors came back today on the basis they think the bolsa's fallen too far," said one broker.
